Written with the smaller number first, {@ansd@}. The strict end and the inclusive end have changed places.[[else]]: {@ansd@}.[[/if]]

(b) The integers are \({@ints@}\): there are \({@cnt@}\) of them. [[if test="lc"]]\({@lo@}\) is included (\(\le\)); [[else]]\({@lo@}\) is not included (\(\lt\)); [[/if]][[if test="rc"]]\({@hi@}\) is included.[[else]]\({@hi@}\) is not included.[[/if]]

questiondescription.text:
Linear Inequalities: solving a compound inequality

Grade 12 CBE Essential 1.3: Solve a compound inequality by doing the same to all three parts, and count the integers that satisfy it.

Essential

This question is adapted from Chapter 28 (Solving inequalities), Section F, questions F5 and F6 of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Higher 1 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2006: new compound inequalities, some with a negative coefficient, entered as number, sign, x, sign, number.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).
